sentence: This project studies how compartments inside a human cell are structured and how protein condensates that form through phase separation govern their interactions.
This project explores a vaccine based on B cells as immunotherapy to treat glioblastoma and other deadly tumors.
This project builds health information tools that gather and summarize patient information so care teams have complete information during care transitions.
This project studies how a herpesvirus that causes Kaposi's sarcoma changes metabolic enzymes in cells through protein phosphorylation.
This project studies how the immune environment of prostate tumors differs between men of African and European ancestry and affects response to immune-modulators.
This project studies which bacterial and host factors affect gastric cancer in people with iron deficiency.
This project supports cystic fibrosis research with biostatistics, study design and computer analysis of large-scale omics data.
This project studies how inherited genetic variants in one gene raise the risk of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
This project offers mass spectrometry methods and related tools for studying cellular metabolism.
This project studies how a protein loses its splicing repression function in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis and Fronto-temporal Dementia to develop a prognostic test.
This project develops gene therapy that edits blood stem cells inside the body to make them resistant to HIV.
This project tests whether blocking a protein in acute myeloid leukemia helps the immune system eliminate leukemia cells.
This project develops a smartphone-based platform that community health workers use to screen people in rural settings for common eye diseases.
This project studies how a choline transporter helps a type of acute myeloid leukemia survive and whether blocking it can suppress cancer cells.
This project tests whether extracellular vesicles from dental pulp stem cells reduce inflammation and apoptosis in retinal ischemia.
This project studies how a membrane transport protein linked to diabetes works in pancreatic islet cells.
This project studies how a structure called the amygdalostriatal transition zone shapes learned responses to stimuli that predict rewards or punishments.
This project studies the gene regulatory controls that let zebrafish repair the heart, to find ways to reprogram human cardioids to regenerate.
This project sets up an instrument that combines optical tweezers with superresolution microscopy to study single molecule force and fluorescence.
This project studies how enveloped viruses such as influenza fuse membranes to enter cells and how avian strains gain the ability to infect humans.
